The United States officially left the gold standard in 1970, when one U.S. dollar was technically worth exactly 1/35 of a troy ounce (889 mg) of gold [4]. However, the country had already suspended the gold standard in 1933, when the government stopped paying gold on demand for the dollar and gold was no longer considered valid legal tender for debts [5].

The Svalbard Global Seed Vault was officially opened on February 26, 2008, although the first seeds arrived in January 2008 [2]. The vault was scheduled to open in late 2008, and it was supported by the Global Crop Diversity Trust and the Nordic Genetic Resource Center (NordGen) [3]. The Norwegian government funded the construction of the vault, which has a storage capacity of 4.5 million seed samples [4].

The national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago, "Forged from the Love of Liberty," was composed by Patrick S. Castagne in 1962, when the song was adopted as the national anthem for the short-lived West Indies Federation [1]. Castagne, a renowned West Indian songwriter, edited and adopted the song after Trinidad and Tobago gained independence on August 31, 1962 [2].

The famous street in New Orleans is Bourbon Street [1], which is a historic street in the French Quarter and is known for its many bars and strip clubs, attracting millions of visitors each year. However, other notable streets in New Orleans include St. Charles Avenue [2], which is famous for its tree-lined boulevard and historic mansions, and Royal Street [3], which is known for its antique shops, art galleries, and hotels.

The singer of the Beatles song "Do You Want to Know a Secret?" is George Harrison [1]. The song was primarily composed by John Lennon, but credited to Lennon–McCartney, and was given to Harrison to sing because it best suited his vocal range [2]. Harrison sang this song, along with "Chains," on the Beatles' album "Please Please Me" [3].

The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, which abolished slavery and involuntary servitude, was ratified by the states on December 6, 1865 [1, 2, 4]. The amendment was passed by Congress on April 8, 1864 (Senate) and January 31, 1865 (House), and was proclaimed adopted by Secretary of State William H. Seward on December 18, 1865 [2, 4].

Michael Jackson's vocals were featured on the song "Don't Matter to Me" from Drake's album "Scorpion" (2018), which was released on July 6, 2018 as the album's fourth single [1]. The song reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart, making it Jackson's 30th top-ten entry [2].
England won the FIFA World Cup in soccer in 1966, defeating West Germany 4-2 in the final, which was held on July 30, 1966, in England [1][2][3].

Booker T. Washington delivered his famous Atlanta Exposition Speech on September 18, 1895, to a predominantly white audience at the Cotton States and International Exposition in Atlanta, Georgia [3], calling for African Americans to join the workforce and submit to white rule in exchange for education and due process [4].
Alabama did not become a right-to-work state. However, neighboring states such as Louisiana did. Louisiana adopted a right-to-work law in 1976 [2][3], and Oklahoma adopted a similar law in 2001 [1].

The first North American Indigenous Games were held in 1990 in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada [1]. However, the idea to hold a multi-sport event for indigenous North American athletes began in the 1970s, with the Native Summer Games held in Enoch, Alberta, Canada in 1971 [2].

The Dark Tower series by Stephen King consists of eight books, which incorporate themes from multiple genres, including dark fantasy, science fantasy, horror, and Western [1]. However, King has stated that the series is actually one long "über-novel" [3], with the seven books being sections of a larger work. The series is part of King's multiverse, linking together many of his other novels and short stories [1].

The Myrtle Beach SkyWheel is located in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, near Plyler Park, and is situated along the city's new boardwalk [2]. It was the tallest Ferris wheel in the United States east of the Mississippi River at the time of its construction, standing at 187 feet [3].

The third season of the animated television series "Rick and Morty" originally aired on Cartoon Network's late-night programming block, Adult Swim, Sundays at 11:30 p.m EST [2]. The season comprised ten episodes and concluded on October 1, 2017 [1].

The term that refers to linking a currency value to the value of gold is the "gold standard" [1]. Under the gold standard, a country's government declares that it will freely exchange currency for actual gold at the designated exchange rate [2]. This monetary system works on the assumption that there are no restrictions on capital movements or export of gold by private citizens across countries.

Soccer was first introduced in the Olympics at the 1900 Summer Olympics, as a contest between two French teams, and at the 1904 Summer Olympics, but it became an official Olympic competition at the 1908 Summer Olympics, where England won the event as the first Olympic football tournament [5].

The Cleveland Browns returned to the NFL in 1999, after a three-year period of deactivation, with the NFL allowing the team to re-establish itself in Cleveland [1]. This move came after the team's previous owner, Art Modell, relocated the franchise to Baltimore in 1996, but retained the Browns' history and colors in Cleveland [2]. The team's return was facilitated by the NFL, which considered the Browns to be a continuation of the previous franchise and retained all team history [3].
St. Petersburg is a city located in Pinellas County, Florida, United States [1]. Specifically, it is situated on the Pinellas peninsula between Tampa and Clearwater [1].

The first handheld camera was introduced by George Eastman in 1888, with the Kodak camera, which was marketed with the slogan "You press the button, we do the rest" [3]. This camera was pre-loaded with a roll of film that produced about 100 2.5" round pictures exposures, and it could easily be carried and handheld during its operation.

Anne Hathaway portrayed the White Queen, also known as Mirana of Marmoreal, in the 2010 adaptation of "Alice Through the Looking Glass" alongside Helena Bonham Carter as Iracebeth, the Red Queen [1]. Hathaway described her interpretation of the White Queen as "a punk-rock vegan pacifist" [2], drawing inspiration from Debbie Harry and the artwork of Dan Flavin. In the film, the White Queen is portrayed as a benevolent and kind character, but with a sadistic side [3].

The Ordinance of Secession was drafted and ratified by the delegates of the people of the state of South Carolina in a general convention on December 20, 1860, with the document being written by Christopher Memminger, who outlined the reasons for secession [1]. However, the actual drafters of the ordinance are not explicitly mentioned in the provided search results.

The total cost for Rio to host the Olympics was estimated at USD 4.6 billion in 2015-dollars [1][4], which includes direct capital costs such as building competition venues, the Olympic village, international broadcast center, and media and press center [1]. This figure is comparable to the costs of other Olympics, such as USD 40-44 billion for Beijing 2008 and USD 51 billion for Sochi 2014 [1].

The festival of Holi marks the end of winter and the beginning of spring, as well as the arrival of new life and colors, and is celebrated as a time of renewal and rejuvenation [2]. It is also observed as a time to say farewell to winter and welcome the fertile land and good spring harvests [3].

The song "Brown Eyes" was written by Christine McVie, and she was one of six songs composed and sung by her in the 1979 double LP "Tusk" [1]. The song was also co-written by Peter Green, who overdubbed electric guitar on the track [1]. The United States purchased the Gadsden Purchase from Mexico, specifically from President Antonio López de Santa Anna, in 1853, with the treaty taking effect on June 8, 1854 [1]. The purchase was signed on December 30, 1853, by James Gadsden, U.S. ambassador to Mexico, and by Antonio López de Santa Anna, president of Mexico [3].

The Royal Flying Doctor Service (RFDS) was established by Reverend John Flynn on May 15, 1928, in Cloncurry, Queensland, as the Australian Inland Mission Aerial Medical Service [1]. This experiment later became The Royal Flying Doctor Service, with the name change occurring in 1942, and the addition of "Royal" in 1955 [3].

The song "Genie in a Bottle" was released on June 22, 1999, by RCA Records as the lead single from Christina Aguilera's self-titled debut album [1]. It reached number one on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and became the biggest summer song of 1999, staying at the top for five consecutive weeks [2]. The success of the song marked the third time that year a new female artist reached number one on the Hot 100 with her debut single [3].

The second season of the Netflix series "Jessica Jones" was released on March 8, 2018, to coincide with International Women's Day [1]. The season was initially planned to be released after the miniseries "The Defenders" in 2017, but was ultimately released in 2018 [2].

The end of Roman rule in Britain is attributed to a combination of factors, including the withdrawal of troops by the usurper Magnus Maximus in 383 and the expulsion of Roman officials by the Romano-Britons in response to a request for aid from Emperor Honorius, which was ultimately rejected [1]. According to historian Michael Jones, the Britons first appealed to Rome for help, but when none was forthcoming, they took charge of their own affairs and expelled the Roman officials [2]. The departure of Roman rule in Britain is seen as a result of a complex interplay of events, with some historians arguing that it was Britain that left Rome, citing poor administration and the rise of usurpers in Britain [5].

The torch at the 2012 Olympics was lit by Sir Steve Redgrave, who received the flame from young footballer Jade Bailey and carried it into the Olympic Stadium [1]. The flame was then passed to seven young athletes, each nominated by a famous British Olympian, who applied their torch to one of the 204 petals [2].

The Latin word "camera obscura" translates to "dark room" [1][3], referring to the natural optical phenomenon where an image is projected through a small hole, forming an inverted image on a surface opposite the opening [1][3]. This concept has been used in various devices, including camera obscura boxes, which were used to expose light-sensitive materials and eventually developed into photographic cameras [4].

The Boston Red Sox set a franchise record for the most games won in a season with 108 victories in the 1912 season, surpassing the previous mark of 105 set in the same year [3]. This record stood for over a century until the 2021 season, when the team won 109 games [not included in the search results, but included for context].
The winner of Britain's Got Talent in 2015 was Jules O'Dwyer & Matisse, a dog tricks duo [1].

The introduction of cricket to India is attributed to the East India Company, which introduced the game to the region in the 17th century [1]. The earliest reference to cricket being played in the Indian sub-continent was in 1721, when British sailors of the East India Company were reported to be playing cricket at Cambay, near Baroda [3]. The Parsi community in India also played a significant role in popularizing the game, with the Oriental Cricket Club being established by the Parsis in Mumbai (formerly Bombay) in 1848 [4].
The original "Baywatch" series featured a character named Matt Brody, played by actor David Charvet [1].

The Black Stallion, a title character from author Walter Farley's bestselling series, was an Arab stallion, while the black stallion mentioned in the first document was a silver stallion, half Quarter Horse and Half Mustang, initially solid black as a colt [1].

The most common type of rock in Earth's crust is igneous rock, which accounts for approximately 64.7% of the Earth's crust by volume [1]. Specifically, the most abundant type of igneous rock is basalt, which is a mafic composition and makes up about 66% of the igneous rocks [1].

The song "Fooled Around and Fell in Love" was written and performed by blues guitarist Elvin Bishop, but he did not sing lead vocals on the track, instead inviting vocalist Mickey Thomas to sing it [1]. The song was released as a single in 1976 and peaked at #3 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 singles chart [1].
The song "As Time Goes By" was written by Herman Hupfeld in 1931 [1][3]. It became most famous in 1942 when part of it was sung by the character Sam in the movie "Casablanca" [1][3].

The systolic blood pressure value is the pressure when the heart is contracting, specifically near the end of the cardiac cycle [1]. This pressure is typically measured using a sphygmomanometer, and the value at which the sound of blood flow begins to be heard through the artery is recorded as the systolic blood pressure [4]. In a normal, resting adult human, the systolic blood pressure is typically around 120 mmHg [1] and [5].
The character Raven, from the TV show "That's So Raven," married a Tamaranean man named General Phy'zzon out of love, after previously being married to Prince Karras to seal a peace treaty [2].
The film "There Will Be Blood" takes place in Southern California during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, specifically in the area of Texas, where the oil boom was taking place [2].

The New York Jets lost the first televised Monday Night Football game to the Cleveland Browns, 31-21 [1]. This historic game aired on September 21, 1970, marking the debut of "Monday Night Football" on ABC [5].

The New England Patriots have won the Super Bowl in a row three times: 2001, 2003, and 2004 [1], and again in 2014 and 2016 [1]. However, the Patriots' streak of winning back-to-back Super Bowls was broken in 2015 when they lost to the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XLIX, but they did win back-to-back Super Bowls in 2003 and 2004 [2], and again in 2014 and 2016 [1].

In the context of networking, NAT stands for Network Address Translation, a method of remapping one IP address space into another by modifying network address information in the IP header of packets [1][2][3]. This technique is used to conserve global address space in the face of IPv4 address exhaustion and is often employed in conjunction with IP masquerading.

The third installment in the "How to Train Your Dragon" series, titled "How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World", was originally scheduled for release on June 17, 2016 [3], but the release date was delayed several times [4]. The film was eventually released on February 22, 2019 [2], after undergoing several changes in its release date.

The song "I'm Not Gonna Miss You" was co-written by Glen Campbell and producer Julian Raymond, and was released on September 30, 2014, for the soundtrack to the documentary "Glen Campbell: I'll Be Me" [1]. The song was nominated for Best Original Song at the 87th Academy Awards, and was performed by Tim McGraw during the ceremony [2].

The role of Cindy Lou Who was played by actress Taylor Momsen in the 2000 live-action film "How the Grinch Stole Christmas!" [1]. However, in the 1966 film adaptation of the book, the role of Cindy Lou was played by actress Angela Lansbury, but in another version of the 1966 film adaptation of the book, the role of Cindy Lou was played by actress Olga James [5].

The ribeye steak comes from the rib section of a beef animal, specifically from the longissimus dorsi muscle, as well as the complexus and spinalis muscles [1]. This cut of beef is located in the upper rib cage area and is known for its marbling of fat, making it suitable for various cooking methods [3]. The ribeye is originally the center portion of the rib steak, without the bone, and is considered a flavorful and tender cut [2].

The Lion King musical premiered on Broadway at the New Amsterdam Theater on October 15, 1997, in previews, with the official opening on November 13, 1997 [1]. The show was a commercial success and is still running on Broadway, having moved to the Minskoff Theatre in 2006 [2]. It is now Broadway's third-longest-running show in history and has grossed over $1 billion [1].

The Golden State Warriors are an American professional basketball team based in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, specifically in Oakland, and play their home games at the Oracle Arena [1][2]. The franchise relocated to the Bay Area in 1962 and adopted its brand name Golden State Warriors in 1971, representing the entire state of California [3].

The music for the film "How to Train Your Dragon" was composed by John Powell, who also composed the score for the film on his own, marking his sixth collaboration with DreamWorks Animation [2]. Powell's score for the film earned him his first Academy Award nomination and his third BAFTA nomination, and won the International Film Music Critics Association 2011 Awards for Best Original Score for an Animated Feature [1].

The first rocket to reach space was the German V-2 rocket, launched on October 3, 1942, which became the first man-made object to enter space [2]. However, earlier attempts by German scientists during World War II also reached space-like altitudes, with one V-2 rocket reaching an altitude of 11 km in March 1942 [2].

Hungry Jack's owns and operates or sub-licenses all of the Burger King/Hungry Jack's restaurants in Australia, with over 390 locations across the country [1]. This makes Hungry Jack's the second largest franchise of Burger King in the world, with over 390 locations in Australia [4].

The song "You Know Better Than I" (also known as "Better Than I") from the 2000 direct-to-video film "Joseph: King of Dreams" is performed by Joseph, with the lyrics speaking to his trust in God and perseverance through difficult times [2]. The song is sung by Joseph, with David Campbell providing the vocals [2][3].

The song "If I Were a Boy" was originally written and recorded by BC Jean, but it was later recorded by American singer Beyoncé for her album "I Am... Sasha Fierce" [1]. The song was initially rejected by Jean's record company, but after Beyoncé recorded her own version, they reached an agreement [1].

The 1999 film "10 Things I Hate About You" takes place in a late-1990s American high school setting, specifically at a school in the Seattle metropolitan area, with many scenes shot at Stadium High School in Tacoma [1]. The story is a loose modernization of William Shakespeare's comedy "The Taming of the Shrew", set in a high school environment [3].

According to the Laws of the Game (2018/19), a player may only be substituted during a stoppage in play and with the permission of the referee [3]. The player to be substituted must have left the field of play before the substitute may enter, and the incoming player may only enter the field at the half-way line or at a goal kick, corner kick, or throw-in [3].
The city in Texas with the highest elevation is El Paso, which is home to the Franklin Mountains State Park, with its highest peak, North Franklin Mountain, reaching an elevation of 7,192 feet [2].

The author of the influential essay "An Essay on the Principle of Population" was Thomas Robert Malthus, who anonymously published the book in 1798 but was soon identified as the author [1]. The essay predicted a grim future due to population growth outpacing food production, unless births were controlled, and was revised for over 28 years [2]. Malthus's work established the field of demography and presented a pivotal approach to examining population growth on a region-by-region basis [4].

Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band played at the halftime show during Super Bowl XLIII in 2009 [1]. The performance was a high-profile event, and it marked one of the few times Springsteen had agreed to play at the Super Bowl, having previously been unsure of its legitimacy [1].

The first season of the BBC's "Sherlock" series consists of three 90-minute episodes, which were initially planned to be broadcast in 2010 [1]. However, the series ultimately consisted of four three-part series airing from 2010 to 2017, with a total of 13 episodes [4].

The movie "Summer of '42" was primarily filmed on Nantucket Island, off the coast of Cape Cod, where the story takes place [2]. However, some interior scenes were likely filmed in other locations, but the exact locations are not specified in the provided documents.

In the TV show "Still Game," Winston buys several electric heaters at an outdoor market in Possilpark [1].

The New York Knicks last won a championship in 1973, defeating the Los Angeles Lakers in a quick 5-game series [2]. This was the second and final NBA title the Knicks would ever win, with Walt Frazier being a member of every championship Knick team in NBA history [2].
The two theme parks at Euro Disney, now known as Disneyland Paris, are Disneyland Park and Walt Disney Studios Park [3].

Ragtime music flourished in the United States in the late 19th century, particularly in the 1890s, as it gained widespread popularity and became mainstream [1]. This period saw the rise of African-American styles, including the cakewalk and ragtime, which were initially associated with poor African Americans but eventually became adopted by Tin Pan Alley [2]. By the start of the 20th century, ragtime had become widely popular throughout North America, with distinctly American musical styles that synthesized African syncopation and European classical music [3].

Yuzuru Hanyu won the gold medal in the men's single figure skating competition at the 2018 Winter Olympics, becoming the first male figure skater to win two consecutive gold medals after Dick Button [1].

The new army uniform, also known as the Army Combat Uniform (ACU), features an Operational Camouflage Pattern (OCP) and was first made available to U.S. Army soldiers on July 1, 2015 [2]. The OCP uniforms began being issued to recruits in basic training and cadets in Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps on October 1, 2019, with all Airmen required to own OCP uniforms by April 1, 2021 [2].

The Philadelphia Phillies won the World Series in 1980, defeating the Kansas City Royals in game 6 on October 21, 1980 [1][3]. They also won the World Series in 2008, defeating their opponent in the series [2][5].
The role of Ingrid on the TV series "Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman" was initially played by Ashley Jones, but later by Jennifer Youngs, who began playing the character from its second appearance [1].

The third season of "RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars" premiered on January 25, 2018 [2].

Piper Chapman is a fictional character played by Taylor Schilling in the Netflix series "Orange Is the New Black", based on the memoir of Piper Kerman [2]. The character is based on Piper Kerman, author of the non-fiction book "", upon which the series is based [3].

The first commercially available cellular phone, the Motorola DynaTAC 8000x, was released in the United States in 1983, with a list price of around $4,000 [2]. However, the first mobile telephone call from a handheld phone was made on April 3, 1973, by Martin Cooper, a Motorola researcher and executive, when he placed a call to Dr. Joel S. Engel of Bell Labs [4].

Creator and writer Chris Chibnall had a "lightbulb moment" and decided that Joe should be the killer, which improved the narrative structure and focused the series on Ellie Miller [2]. The reveal of Joe as the murderer was watched by a peak of 9.3 million viewers, but only 7.9 million viewers remained with the episode after the reveal [3].

In the Hannah Montana series, Miley Stewart chooses Jake over Jesse [1][2]. The choice is made in the episode "He Could Be The One," where Miley believes Jake could be the one she is looking for [2].

They were originally named Gregory and Matthew in the pilot, but were later changed to Geoffrey and Michael [5]. The twins were played by child actors Sawyer and Sullivan Sweeten [2].

The song "Next to Me" by Imagine Dragons features the lead vocals of Dan Reynolds [1]. The song was released on February 21, 2018, as the fourth single from the band's third studio album "Evolve" [2].

One pioneer in the field of eyewitness research is Gary L. Wells, a psychologist who has made significant contributions to understanding the reliability of eyewitness testimony [2]. His work, including a chapter on "Eyewitness identification research" with Steven D. Penrod, has evaluated alternative research methods and provided insights into the strengths and weaknesses of various approaches [2]. Additionally, Wells has developed Bayesian methods to assess the impact of eyewitness identification evidence, highlighting the importance of considering other evidence in court [2].

The Shema is found in the Torah in Deuteronomy 6:4-9, 11:13-21, and Numbers 15:37-41 [1]. These sections are also mentioned in the Mishnah (Berachot 2:2) as the three portions that relate to central issues of Jewish belief [2]. The recitation of the Shema in the liturgy consists of these three portions, which are already mentioned in the Mishnah (Berachot 2:5) as part of the daily prayer services [3].

Michael Jordan's last year with the Chicago Bulls was the 1997-1998 season [1], during which the team won their sixth championship in eight years [2]. Jordan announced his second retirement after the season, marking the end of the Bulls' dynasty [3].

The first Krispy Kreme store was located in a rented building on South Main Street in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, in what is now called historic Old Salem [1]. This location was established by Vernon Rudolph in 1937, after he had decided to open the first Krispy Kreme in Winston-Salem due to the presence of Camel cigarettes in the city [2].

The Tin Woodman, a character in the classic film "The Wizard of Oz," claims to have no heart [1]. However, the song "If I Only Had a Heart" suggests that he may be longing for a heart, implying that he may indeed have one [2].

A standard match in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege typically lasts four minutes for a casual mode and three minutes for a competitive mode [2]. However, the overall gameplay session can last significantly longer, with some players reportedly spending up to 24 real-time hours playing the game [4].
The 2016 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship was won by O'Loughlin Gaels, who defeated Ballyhale Shamrocks 0-19 to 1-12 in the final [1].

The instrument that you blow into with a keyboard is the melodica, also known as the pianica or blow-organ [4]. It has a musical keyboard on top and is played by blowing air through a mouthpiece that fits into a hole in the side of the instrument, similar to a wind controller [1].

After the death of Qutub ud din Aibak, his successor was Shams ud-Din Iltutmish [1], who was a slave general of Ghori and had been given the responsibility of governing the conquered territories of India [2].

There were 8 teams in the NBA in 1956, consisting of the New York Knicks, Boston Celtics, Philadelphia Warriors, Minneapolis Lakers, Rochester Royals, Fort Wayne Pistons, Tri-Cities Blackhawks, and Syracuse Nationals [3].

The character of the older Dottie Hinson in the 1992 film "A League of Their Own" was played by Lynn Cartwright [1]. However, the character of Dottie Hinson was loosely based on Dottie Kamenshek, a real-life professional baseball catcher for the Rockford Peaches in the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League [4].

Neil Armstrong received the Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Richard Nixon [3], as did his Apollo 11 crewmates, in recognition of their historic achievement of the first manned Moon landing [5].

The song "(Remember Me) I'm the One Who Loves You" was written and originally sung by Stuart Hamblen in 1950 [1]. It was also a hit for Ernest Tubb the same year, and Dean Martin released a version of the song in 1965, which spent 7 weeks on the "Billboard" Hot 100 chart, peaking at No. 32 [5].

The only child of a president to be born in the White House was Esther Cleveland, the daughter of President Grover Cleveland, born on September 9, 1893 [1]. She was the second child of the president, and her birth in the White House made her a unique figure in American history.

To change a lead atom into a gold atom, a process of nuclear transmutation would be required, which involves altering the atomic nucleus by removing or adding protons and neutrons [3]. This can be achieved through the use of particle accelerators or nuclear reactors, as demonstrated by Glenn Seaborg's experiment in 1980, where he transmuted several thousand atoms of bismuth into gold [3]. However, this process is highly expensive and not feasible for routine manufacture of gold [3].

Michael Moriarty, the actor who portrayed Ben Stone on the TV drama "Law & Order", left the show in 1994 [3]. His departure from the series was reportedly due to his dispute with the network and U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno [2]. This occurred at the end of season four, which aired between September 15, 1993, and May 25, 1994 [4].

The Straits of Mackinac connects Lake Michigan and Lake Huron, creating a single lake, and they meet at this point [1]. The combined waters of Lake Michigan and Lake Huron have the same surface elevation due to the free exchange of water between the two sides through the Straits [2].

The day of Sunday became the seventh day of the week with the decree of Roman emperor Constantine in AD 321, when he established Sunday as a day of rest from labor [3]. This change was further solidified by the Council of Laodicea in 363, which prohibited observance of the Jewish Sabbath (Saturday) and encouraged Christians to work on Saturday and rest on Sunday [5].

The song "Fairytale of New York" was written by Jem Finer and Shane MacGowan, and recorded by the Pogues, featuring singer-songwriter Kirsty MacColl on vocals [1].
